chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have dependents, and upon me is a debt, and my condition has become difficult, so teach me a supplication; when I supplicate with it, Allah will grant me sustenance by which I can pay off my debt and assist my dependents with it.'

So he said, 'O servant of Allah! Perform ablution and perfect your ablution, then pray two rak'ahs, completing the bowing and prostration in them, then say: 'O Glorious! O One! O Generous! I turn to You through Muhammad, Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy. O Muhammad! O Messenger of Allah! I turn through You to Allah, Your Lord and the Lord of all things, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his Ahl al-Bayt. And I ask You for a breath from Your breaths, and an easy opening, and abundant sustenance, by which I may gather my scattered affairs, pay off my debt, and assist my dependents.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for paying off debt and gaining sustenance according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the 'Salat al-Hajah' (Prayer of Need) as a structured spiritual remedy for financial anxiety, emphasizing the intercessory role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his Ahl al-Bayt. The supplication highlights the Shia theological concept of *tawassul*, where believers seek nearness to Allah through the Prophet's merit to secure *rizq* (sustenance) and alleviate worldly burdens.
